title: Change Email: Let Users Update Their Email Address

chapters.title: Users Change Email
chapters.subtitle: Let users update their own email address

steps.text: Users Change Email is an Orchard Core feature that lets each signed-in user change the email address of their own account. In this video, you enable it, turn on its setting, and follow a user through the change.

chapters.title: What the feature adds
chapters.subtitle: A separate way to change an email address

steps.text: By default, the Email field on the edit page of an existing user can't be edited. The User Login setting, Allow user to change their email address, makes that field editable.
The Users Change Email feature adds another way: a Change Email item in the user menu, and a page where a signed-in user types a different address. A site setting turns both on or off.
This is the Features page, under Tools. Let's search for change email. The feature is called Users Change Email, and it's listed in the Security category.
Select Enable. A message confirms that the feature Users Change Email was enabled.
This is Settings, Security, Change Email. Enabling the feature isn't enough: until the setting is on, the user menu doesn't show the item, and the Change Email page returns not found.
Check Allow the users to change their email, and select Save. The setting applies to every user of the site.
A message confirms it: Site settings updated successfully. Clearing the checkbox hides the item and the page again, while the feature stays enabled.
This is the Users list, under Access Control. Any signed-in user can change their own address. In the admin, the user menu is the user icon in the top bar.
The menu starts with Signed in as, followed by the user name. Change Email is listed between Change password and Log off. Let's select it.
The Change Email page has one field, Email, filled with the current address of the account. Let's replace it with a different address.
Select Submit. The Email changed page thanks the user. The address is saved as soon as the form is submitted: the form asks for the address only, and the module doesn't ask the user to confirm it.
Back on the Users list, the row of the user shows the replacement address next to the user name. At sign-in, the user can also type that address in the Username or email address field.
The page checks an address before it saves it. If the address is the one the account already has, the page answers: This email is already your current one.
If another user already has the address, the page answers: A user with the same email already exists.
A value that isn't an email address is refused with a validation message. In each case, the address of the account stays as it was.

chapters.title: Summary
chapters.subtitle: Enable it, allow it, use it

steps.text: To sum up: enable the feature, turn on the setting, and users choose Change Email in their menu. When the Deployment feature is enabled, a deployment step called Change Email settings exports the setting.
That's Users Change Email: a menu item and a page that let signed-in users keep their own email address up to date. Thanks for watching.
